doc.title: Ellis Marsalis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 7, 2020

title: Harold Batiste as mentor teaching chord basics
summary: Harold Batiste, three years older and at Dillard, taught him chord changes and voicings.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Okay. So at that time if you wondered what is a B flat 13 chord, where did you go to find that information?

Harold Batiste was a mentor for me. He was about three years older than me. He went to Dillard University and had been there maybe three years, and I went as a freshman. And he was a mentor for me in terms of saying this is chord changes, you know, this is like C7, this is how you voice that. A lot of very basic stuff.

I’m glad you told me that. It’s interesting that mentors don’t have to be a lot older than you, right? I mean when you’re that age, three years seems like a long time but then later on it’s not. But wow. I think I saw him years ago at a concert. It was very, very interesting. And you had a big decision to make about the military? You ended up joining the Marine Corps?
